# 单篇讲义生成任务

项目仓库: adam-maj/tiny-gpu
项目名: tiny-gpu
讲义目录: tiny-gpu-tutorial/
代码永久链接 base: https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/
当前 HEAD: 02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2
动作: new


---

## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论）

# 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你不能：

- 修改源码
- 写入任何 `.md` 文件
- 输出 JSON 以外的文字

你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。

---

## 总目标

为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。

这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。

每篇讲义应该满足：

1. 面向初学者也能读懂。
2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。
3. 必须结合真实源码。
4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。

---

## 源码探查顺序

请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节：

1. 项目说明
   - README
   - docs
   - examples
   - tutorials

2. 构建与运行方式
   - package.json
   - Cargo.toml
   - pyproject.toml
   - go.mod
   - pom.xml
   - Makefile
   - Dockerfile
   - CI 配置

3. 项目入口
   - CLI 入口
   - Web 服务入口
   - main 文件
   - library export 文件
   - examples 入口

4. 目录结构
   - src
   - lib
   - app
   - packages
   - crates
   - tests

5. 核心流程
   - 初始化流程
   - 配置加载
   - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路
   - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制

6. 测试与示例
   - 单元测试
   - 集成测试
   - benchmark
   - example usage

---

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 项目概览：tiny-gpu 是什么

本讲为整本手册入门篇，不涉电路细节，依据 README.md 建立学习坐标。核心结论：tiny-gpu 是用 Verilog/SystemVerilog（硬件描述语言）写成的教学型最小 GPU，专为「从零理解 GPU 硬件」优化，区别于追求功能完整的开源 GPU（Miaow、VeriGPU）。

关键概念：须区分 GPU 编程（软件层，如 CUDA）与 GPU 硬件（电路层），本项目只攻后者，kernel 指运行在 GPU 上的代码。三大学习主题——架构、并行化、内存——是后续单元主线，递进关系为：拆分部件→core 内并行→内存带宽成瓶颈需控制器节流；并行的根基是 SIMD（单指令多数据）。源码为 src/ 下约 12 个 .sv 文件，覆盖顶层、派发、core、内存控制器及取指/译码/ALU/访存/寄存器/PC 等部件。

简化是项目「tiny」之本：一次单 kernel、数据与程序内存分离且容量小、cache 仅占位、PC 收敛假设（即忽略分支分歧 branch divergence）、无流水线、无 warp 调度；这些被砍掉的优化正是真实 GPU 重点，留待 Unit 7 讨论。
### u1-l2 仓库结构与源码地图

本讲是 tiny-gpu 的「地图篇」，建立文件、模块与架构图的对照表。仓库分四部分：src/ 存 12 个 SystemVerilog 硬件源码，test/ 是 cocotb Python 仿真测试台，docs/images/ 放架构图，gds/ 为流片版图产物。源码围绕 GPU→Core→Thread 三层结构组织：顶层 gpu 实例化 dcr（设备控制寄存器，存 thread_count）、两次 controller（分别服务 data 与只读 program 内存）、dispatch 派发器，以及由 generate 循环复制的 NUM_CORES 个 core；每个 core 含单实例的 fetcher/decoder/scheduler，再用 generate 循环为每线程复制一套 alu/lsu/registers/pc，共 12 个模块、无孤儿文件。引入的关键术语包括：module（带端口的电路积木）、instantiation（实例化）、generate 循环（编译期复制电路）、cocotb（用 Python 驱动 iverilog 仿真）。.sv 是被测对象、由 iverilog 执行，.py 是测试台，二者不可混淆；线程以 enable 门控，只有前 thread_count 个硬件真正工作。学习要诀是「图先行、再回源码印证」。
### u1-l3 构建与仿真工具链

本讲解決 tiny-gpu 的 SystemVerilog 源码如何跑起来。仿真工具链由 sv2v（SystemVerilog→Verilog）、iverilog（编译成 build/sim.vvp）、vvp（运行仿真）、cocotb（Python 测试台，经 VPI 驱动）四件工具串联。入口 make test_<名字> 命中 Makefile 的 test_% 模式规则（用 $* 取「茎」），依次执行 compile→iverilog→vvp 三步。compile 中 sv2v -I src/* 会吃掉字母序最前的 alu.sv，故 alu 须经 compile_% 规则单独编译、再 cat 拼回 build/gpu.v 并在顶部补 timescale；iverilog 用 -s gpu 指定顶层模块。cocotb 靠 libcocotbvpi_icarus 与 LIBPYTHON_LOC 搭起 Python↔Verilog 桥。测试台 setup.py 启动序列为建时钟、复位、装程序与数据内存、写设备控制寄存器（设 thread_count）、拉 start，主循环用 RisingEdge(dut.clk) 逐拍同步、每拍驱动一次外部内存。日志写入 test/logs/log_<时间戳>.txt，分「初始数据内存」「执行轨迹」「最终数据内存」三段，内存表标题为 DATA MEMORY。引入的关键术语：仿真器、testbench、VPI、模式规则、DCR、start/done。
### u2-l1 gpu.sv 顶层架构

本讲义只拆解 tiny-gpu 的顶层模块 `gpu.sv` 的「连线」，不进入任何子模块内部。核心结论有四点：第一，顶层用 8 个 `parameter` 把数据内存规格（8 位地址/8 位数据/4 通道）、程序内存规格（8 位地址/16 位指令/1 通道）、`NUM_CORES`、`THREADS_PER_BLOCK` 全部参数化，并用 `localparam` 派生出 `NUM_LSUS = NUM_CORES × THREADS_PER_BLOCK` 与 `NUM_FETCHERS = NUM_CORES`。第二，顶层端口分四类：`clk/reset`、内核生命周期握手 `start/done`、DCR 写入接口、以及两套多通道 `valid/ready/data` 内存握手接口（程序内存只读、数据内存可读写）。第三，顶层实例化 4 类子模块：`dcr`（产出 thread_count）、两个 `controller`（数据控制器接 8 个 LSU/4 通道、程序控制器接 2 个 fetcher/1 通道且 `WRITE_ENABLE=0`）、`dispatch`（派发 block 并汇总 done）。第四，`NUM_CORES` 个 core 由 `generate for` 展开；为兼容 Verilog 2005 不能切片顶层信号的限制，每核先接本地 `core_lsu_*`，再用 `always @(posedge clk)` 按 `i*THREADS_PER_BLOCK+j` 重排下标穿透到顶层 `lsu_*` 数组，该寄存器赋值引入 1 拍延迟；fetcher 侧每核仅 1 个，直接对接无需中间寄存器。引入并供后续讲义承接的关键术语：parameter/localparam 参数化、unpackaged 多通道数组端口、`consumer_*`/`mem_*`/`lsu_*`/`fetcher_*` 命名约定、generate 多核展开、LSU/fetcher 穿透寄存器及其延迟。
### u2-l2 内核启动：DCR 与 Dispatcher

本讲解析内核启动的最小模块 DCR（dcr.sv）与 Dispatcher（dispatch.sv），由顶层 gpu.sv 串接。DCR 是一个 8 位寄存器，主机经 write_enable + data 写入 thread_count（非阻塞赋值，下一拍才生效），设定本次内核线程数。Dispatcher 按向上取整式 total_blocks = (thread_count + TPB - 1) / TPB 把线程切成 block，每拍执行「派发 + 回收」两个循环：向 core_reset=1 的空闲核派发 block，并回收 core_start && core_done 的核以复用。关键术语包括：thread_count、THREADS_PER_BLOCK（TPB）、block、total_blocks、core_reset/core_start/core_done 握手信号，以及 blocks_dispatched / blocks_done 计数器。核心结论：派发用阻塞赋值使一拍内能向多核依次派不同 block，控制信号用非阻塞故下一拍才对 core 生效；最后一块走尾数分支 thread_count - blocks_dispatched*TPB；done 在所有 block 收回、blocks_done==total_blocks 命中后下一拍才拉高。core_done 源自 core 内 scheduler 跑到 RET 指令，其内部状态机细节留待后续讲义展开。
### u3-l1 内存模型与外部接口

本讲确立 tiny-gpu 与外部内存的边界约定。设有两块独立内存：data 内存（8 位地址、8 位数据、4 通道，可读写）与 program 内存（8 位地址、16 位指令、1 通道，只读），规格全部由 gpu.sv 的 parameter 定义。对外采用统一的「多通道 valid/ready/data」握手：请求类信号（valid/address/write-data）为 GPU 输出，应答类信号（ready/read-data）为 GPU 输入。两块内存各由一个 controller 实例作中继——data 控制器在 8 个 LSU 与 4 个外部通道间仲裁，program 控制器服务 2 个 fetcher、1 通道且 WRITE_ENABLE=0。仿真中外部内存由 Python 的 Memory 类扮演，每拍 run() 一次、零延迟同拍响应；因 cocotb 将多通道信号序列化为拼接长串，run() 须逐位/逐段解析请求，再以同一布局把应答拼回写回 DUT。load() 灌入初始数据、display() 打印内存表格以供观察。controller 内部仲裁逻辑留待 u3-l2。
### u3-l2 内存控制器：带宽节流

本讲拆解 tiny-gpu 内存控制器 `controller.sv`。它存在的根本原因是带宽瓶颈：消费者（data 控制器 8 个 LSU、program 控制器 2 个 fetcher）多于外部通道（4 条、1 条），均 2 倍过订阅，需一个仲裁中继者把 N 路请求节流到 M 条通道。每条通道独立跑一份五态状态机 `IDLE/READ_WAITING/WRITE_WAITING/READ_RELAYING/WRITE_RELAYING`，由外层 `for i` 并发驱动；`IDLE` 按消费者编号做固定优先级轮询，配 `break` 保证「一通道一周期一请求」。关键术语包括规模参数 `NUM_CONSUMERS/NUM_CHANNELS/WRITE_ENABLE`；跨通道去重锁 `channel_serving_consumer` 的置位/复位用阻塞赋值 `=` 使「领走/释放」同周期内即时可见，而数据通路用非阻塞 `<=` 保持同步时序，体现「协调用阻塞、数据用非阻塞」的混合用法；`current_consumer[i]` 作回执地址，把外部应答精确扔回当初的消费者，读回传数据、写只回确认。核心结论：中继时序上 `WAITING` 等的是外部内存（零延迟约 1 拍），`RELAYING` 等的是消费者撤回 valid（约 2 拍）。本讲只聚焦控制器本身，不涉及 LSU/fetcher 内部状态机及缓存合并等优化。
### u4-l1 Core 解剖结构

本讲只拆解 `core.sv` 一个文件的内部连线，确立 core「一次处理一个 block」的工作模型：dispatcher 派活时递上 `block_id`（映射为 `%blockIdx`）和 `thread_count` 两项 block 元数据。core 内部由三类部件构成：一是**单实例三剑客**——fetcher（取指）、decoder（译码）、scheduler（驱动 `core_state` 七阶段状态机 IDLE→FETCH→DECODE→REQUEST→WAIT→EXECUTE→UPDATE→DONE），它们对应「单指令流」，产出的控制信号（`core_state`、`instruction`、`decoded_*`）被全 core 广播共享；二是**每线程一份**的 ALU/LSU/registers（16 个寄存器，`%threadIdx` 复位为线程号 i）/PC，由 `generate for` 在编译期复制 `THREADS_PER_BLOCK` 套，对应「多数据」。硬件虽建满最大容量，但运行时用 `enable = (i < thread_count)` 门控冻结多余执行单元。两类部件由中间信号缝合：`rs[i]/rt[i]`（registers→ALU/LSU）、`alu_out[i]`（ALU→registers/PC）、`lsu_out[i]`（LSU→registers），在 `core_state` 调度下分 REQUEST/EXECUTE/UPDATE 三拍流动，形成每个线程内 registers↔ALU↔LSU 的闭合数据环路。本讲不展开各子模块内部实现，留待后续讲义。
### u4-l2 Scheduler 核心状态机

scheduler 是 tiny-gpu core 的「指挥」，不参与计算与访存，只把执行一条指令切成七阶段状态机（IDLE→FETCH→DECODE→REQUEST→WAIT→EXECUTE→UPDATE→DONE），用 3 位信号 `core_state` 广播给 fetcher / decoder / LSU / ALU / PC，后者各在自己所属节拍工作——这正是 SIMD 单指令流驱动多线程的硬件体现。其工作粒度是一个 block，从 PC=0 跑到 RET 为止。两类阶段判然分明：DECODE / REQUEST / EXECUTE / UPDATE 是单周期同步推进，根源是非阻塞赋值 `<=` 引入的 1 拍延迟，对所有指令一视同仁；FETCH 与 WAIT 则是变长握手等待。FETCH 靠 `fetcher_state==FETCHED` 与 fetcher 做双向握手；WAIT 用 `for`+`break` 轮询所有线程的 `lsu_state`，只要任一 LSU 仍处 REQUESTING/WAITING 就继续等，因而成为同步指令（1 拍放行）与异步访存（等最慢线程内存往返）的分水岭。UPDATE 阶段以 `current_pc <= next_pc[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1]` 推进 PC，隐含所有线程 PC 相同的「PC 收敛假设」（忽略分支分歧），遇 RET 则置 `done` 进 DONE。单条指令耗时为 `T_inst = t_FETCH + t_WAIT + 4`，解释了内存密集型内核为何更慢。后续讲义将承接 `core_state` 译码、LSU 四态机、寄存器堆写回以及分支分歧等被简化的话题。
### u4-l3 Fetcher 与 Decoder

本讲聚焦 core 单指令流的取指与译码。fetcher 是 IDLE→FETCHING→FETCHED 三态状态机，经 valid/ready 握手从只读程序内存异步取回当前 PC 处的 16 位指令，在 FETCHING→FETCHED 边界锁存进 instruction 寄存器，且译码期间不清零。指令为 16 位定长编码：[15:12]=opcode、[11:8]=rd、[7:4]=rs、[3:0]=rt，而 nzp([11:9])、imm([7:0]) 复用上述字段，含义由 opcode 决定。decoder 在 DECODE 拍纯组合切字段，并「先清零、后 case 查表」拉高一排 decoded_* 控制信号（写回/算术/访存/比较/跳转各类 mux 与 enable）。核心结论：scheduler 广播的 core_state 充当节拍器，分别选通 fetcher（FETCH 拍）与 decoder（DECODE 拍），使单实例取指译码部件与每线程一份的 ALU/LSU/registers/PC 严格同步，构成 SIMD 的硬件基础；控制信号如何被消费留给后续讲义。
### u5-l1 指令集（ISA）与编码

本讲从「指令本身长什么样」切入，给出 tiny-gpu 指令集架构（ISA）的完整契约。核心模块有四：其一，ISA 仅含 11 条指令，分跳转类（BRnzp、RET）、比较类（CMP）、算术类（ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV）、访存常数类（LDR/STR/CONST）及 NOP，操作码在 decoder.sv 用 localparam 写死，是整份指令集的单一事实来源，属 load-store 架构。其二，指令为 16 位定长，切成 opcode[15:12]/rd[11:8]/rs[7:4]/rt[3:0] 四段；位域可被复用，opcode 决定同一字段作寄存器号还是立即数或 nzp 条件位。其三，16 个寄存器中 R0–R12 自由读写，R13–R15 为只读的 %blockIdx/%blockDim/%threadIdx，由硬件 rd<13 写回保护，是 SIMD 让同一段代码处理不同数据的命脉。其四，BRnzp 是唯一控制流指令，用 [11:9] 作 nzp 掩码、[7:0] 作跳转目标，与 CMP 写入的 NZP 寄存器逐位与来决定是否跳转。format.py 的 format_instruction 则是 decoder 的逆运算，用于反汇编与编码验证。
### u5-l2 ALU 与比较/NZP

本讲深入 `alu.sv`，定位 ALU 在 core 数据通路中的角色：它以 `rs/rt` 为输入、`alu_out` 为单出口，处在 registers→ALU→registers/pc 的闭环中，算术结果写回 `rd`，CMP 结果抄入 NZP 寄存器。核心是两只由 decoder 产生的控制阀门：2 位 `decoded_alu_arithmetic_mux` 在 ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV 间四选一；`decoded_alu_output_mux` 在算术模式与比较模式间切换。CMP 模式下 `alu_out[2:0]` 按 N/Z/P 编码：bit[0]=小于、bit[1]=相等、bit[2]=大于。关键结论是：因 rs/rt 为 8 位无符号数，`rs-rt` 不够减时回绕成大正数，使 N 位结构性地恒为 0，故 CMP 实际只能分辨「相等/不等」，无法判定大小方向。时序上 ALU 受 `enable` 与 `core_state==EXECUTE` 双重门控，输出经 `alu_out_reg` 寄存带来 1 拍延迟，形成「EXECUTE 算、UPDATE 用」的节拍咬合。matmul 的 `CMP+BRn` 计数循环正是靠相等/不等判定工作，「负数回绕」非但不是缺陷，反而是循环正确运行的机制。
### u5-l3 LSU 异步访存

本讲围绕 tiny-gpu 的访存执行单元 LSU（Load-Store Unit，`src/lsu.sv`）展开，核心是讲清为何访存需要独立的状态机。算术指令（ADD/SUB 等）在 `EXECUTE` 一拍内自给自足完成；而 LDR/STR 的数据在 core 外部的 data 内存中，需经 LSU→controller→外部内存→controller→LSU 的链路往返，耗时不确定，故须用 `valid/ready` 握手并靠状态机「记住」未完成的请求。LSU 采用 `IDLE→REQUESTING→WAITING→DONE` 四态 FSM（编码 00/01/10/11），由 scheduler 的 `core_state` 门控：`REQUEST` 触发 `IDLE→REQUESTING`，`UPDATE` 复位 `DONE→IDLE`。LDR（读地址=rs）在 `WAITING` 收到 `mem_read_ready` 时把 `mem_read_data` 锁入 `lsu_out`，于 `UPDATE` 写回 `rd`；STR（写地址=rs、写数据=rt）在 `WAITING` 仅撤 `valid`、不写 `lsu_out`——因数据是流出而非回流。`lsu_out` 因此是 LDR 专用的数据出口。scheduler 在 `WAIT` 阶段逐线程轮询 `lsu_state`，凡仍处 `REQUESTING/WAITING` 即原地等待，从而把变长的访存延迟吸收掉；`mem_read_ready`/`mem_write_ready` 则由 controller 中继外部内存应答返回。本讲引入的关键术语：LSU、`lsu_state` 四态、`lsu_out`、core_state 门控、三方握手（scheduler×LSU×controller），为后续寄存器堆与内存优化讲义承接。
### u5-l4 寄存器堆与程序计数器

本讲拆解每线程的寄存器堆（registers.sv）与程序计数器（pc.sv）。寄存器堆含16个8位寄存器：R0–R12自由读写，R13–R15为只读身份寄存器 %blockIdx/%blockDim/%threadIdx，写回时以地址 <13 做硬件保护；它在 REQUEST 阶段读出源操作数 rs/rt，UPDATE 阶段经 reg_input_mux 三路写回（算术←alu_out、访存←lsu_out、常数←立即数）。%blockIdx 每周期无条件刷新为外部 block_id，以冗余写入换取 dispatcher 切换 block 无需重新复位的简单性。PC 在 EXECUTE 阶段计算 next_pc：默认 PC+1，BRnzp 按 (nzp & decoded_nzp)!=0 决定是否跳到立即数。NZP 是粘性信箱，由 CMP 在 UPDATE 写入、由 BRnzp 在 EXECUTE 读取，因阶段错位而天然完成跨指令的比较-跳转交接。current_pc 全 core 共享（单指令流），next_pc 每线程一份但被 PC 收敛假设统一取末尾线程值。
### u6-l1 cocotb 仿真测试框架

本讲把视角从「硬件内部」转向「测试台如何调度硬件」。cocotb 让 Python 充当 testbench，`.sv` 充当被测设计（DUT），二者经 VPI 桥（`libcocotbvpi_icarus`）通信；测试函数是 async 协程，靠 `await` 一个 trigger 把控制权交还仿真器、与硬件同步节拍。核心是 `setup()` 的五步启动序列：建时钟（用 `start_soon` 把方波分叉到后台）、复位脉冲、`load` 装填内存、写 DCR 锁存 `thread_count`、拉 `start` 点火——凡涉 DUT 寄存器都需 `await RisingEdge`，而 `load` 是纯 Python 操作无需等时钟。重点是主循环 `while dut.done.value != 1` 每拍执行 `run()`→`ReadOnly`→`format_cycle`→`RisingEdge`，对应 cocotb 一个周期内 ReadWrite（可写，`Memory.run()` 在此回送多通道内存应答）与 ReadOnly（只读，`format_cycle` 读快照）两阶段，顺序不可颠倒。`Memory` 类以 Python 列表扮演外部 DRAM，每拍零延迟同拍响应；循环退出后由 `assert` 判定成败，轨迹经 `logger.py` 写入带时间戳的 `test/logs/`。引入术语 DUT、VPI、trigger、ReadWrite/ReadOnly、DCR、done，为 u6-l2 执行轨迹阅读与 u6-l3 编写新内核承接。
### u6-l2 执行轨迹格式化与阅读

本讲承接 u6-l1，讲解 cocotb 仿真执行轨迹（execution trace）如何从 DUT 信号翻译为可读日志，主角为 format.py 与 logger.py。核心结论：所有轨迹只写入带时间戳的日志文件、终端无输出。format_cycle 按「cycle→core→thread→字段」四层遍历，每 core 仅读一次 instruction 供全部线程共享（体现 SIMD 单指令流），用核级、线程级与 thread_id 三重过滤控制日志体量，并以 reg_input_mux 选择性打印即将写回的值。关键术语：format_instruction（decoder 逆运算）、四张状态映射表（镜像硬件 localparam，需双向同步）、format_registers（用 reg_idx=15-i 加 reverse 还原 cocotb 倒序遍历的寄存器升序）。字段分 core 共享（PC/Core State/Instruction/Fetcher State）与每线程（Registers/LSU State/RS/RT）两组，是 SIMD 架构的文本投影。两处陷阱：BRnzp 的 nzp 段因字符串与整数比较恒空；format_memory_controller_state 虽定义却从未被调用，属死代码。
### u6-l3 编写与仿真内核

本讲是 Unit 6 的应用篇，承接 u6-l1（驱动硬件）与 u6-l2（读轨迹），讲解如何往 tiny-gpu 塞入自写内核并验证。核心结论：跑内核需备齐「三要素」——程序内存（手工编码的 16 位指令列表）、数据内存（初始数据列表）、线程数（写入 DCR）；README 里的 `.threads`/`.data` 伪指令只供人读，真正生效的是 `test_*.py` 中的 Python 列表，项目并无汇编器。`matadd` 内核演示了 SIMD 主线：用只读寄存器 `%blockIdx/%blockDim/%threadIdx` 算出全局线程号 `i`，按 `baseA/baseB/baseC` 三段布局定位数据，用 `LDR rd,rs`（取 mem[rs] 写 rd）读、`STR rs,rt`（把 rt 写入 mem[rs]，地址/数据字段方向与 LDR 相反）写。`matmul` 内核首次引入循环控制：`CMP`+`BRn` 实现累加循环；关键反直觉点是，因 8 位无符号减法回绕，`CMP` 的 bit[2] 实际等价于「不相等」，`BRn`（掩码 `100`）据此在 `k≠N` 时跳回，行为上等价于「k<N 则循环」，`k==N` 退出。该内核所有线程分支均收敛，满足 scheduler 的「PC 收敛假设」（为 u7-l1 讨论分支分歧埋下伏笔）。校验环节：数据内存分段使输入/输出区不重叠，仿真后用 `data_memory.memory[i+baseC]` 取回结果，与 Python 独立重算的期望值 `assert` 比对；`display` 只写日志供人看，`assert` 才决定成败。写新内核固定五步：设计汇编→手工编码→填 `test_*.py` 三要素→`setup`+主循环→`assert` 校验。

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 项目概览：tiny-gpu 是什么

本讲为整本手册入门篇，不涉电路细节，依据 README.md 建立学习坐标。核心结论：tiny-gpu 是用 Verilog/SystemVerilog（硬件描述语言）写成的教学型最小 GPU，专为「从零理解 GPU 硬件」优化，区别于追求功能完整的开源 GPU（Miaow、VeriGPU）。

关键概念：须区分 GPU 编程（软件层，如 CUDA）与 GPU 硬件（电路层），本项目只攻后者，kernel 指运行在 GPU 上的代码。三大学习主题——架构、并行化、内存——是后续单元主线，递进关系为：拆分部件→core 内并行→内存带宽成瓶颈需控制器节流；并行的根基是 SIMD（单指令多数据）。源码为 src/ 下约 12 个 .sv 文件，覆盖顶层、派发、core、内存控制器及取指/译码/ALU/访存/寄存器/PC 等部件。

简化是项目「tiny」之本：一次单 kernel、数据与程序内存分离且容量小、cache 仅占位、PC 收敛假设（即忽略分支分歧 branch divergence）、无流水线、无 warp 调度；这些被砍掉的优化正是真实 GPU 重点，留待 Unit 7 讨论。
### u1-l2 仓库结构与源码地图

本讲是 tiny-gpu 的「地图篇」，建立文件、模块与架构图的对照表。仓库分四部分：src/ 存 12 个 SystemVerilog 硬件源码，test/ 是 cocotb Python 仿真测试台，docs/images/ 放架构图，gds/ 为流片版图产物。源码围绕 GPU→Core→Thread 三层结构组织：顶层 gpu 实例化 dcr（设备控制寄存器，存 thread_count）、两次 controller（分别服务 data 与只读 program 内存）、dispatch 派发器，以及由 generate 循环复制的 NUM_CORES 个 core；每个 core 含单实例的 fetcher/decoder/scheduler，再用 generate 循环为每线程复制一套 alu/lsu/registers/pc，共 12 个模块、无孤儿文件。引入的关键术语包括：module（带端口的电路积木）、instantiation（实例化）、generate 循环（编译期复制电路）、cocotb（用 Python 驱动 iverilog 仿真）。.sv 是被测对象、由 iverilog 执行，.py 是测试台，二者不可混淆；线程以 enable 门控，只有前 thread_count 个硬件真正工作。学习要诀是「图先行、再回源码印证」。
### u1-l3 构建与仿真工具链

本讲解決 tiny-gpu 的 SystemVerilog 源码如何跑起来。仿真工具链由 sv2v（SystemVerilog→Verilog）、iverilog（编译成 build/sim.vvp）、vvp（运行仿真）、cocotb（Python 测试台，经 VPI 驱动）四件工具串联。入口 make test_<名字> 命中 Makefile 的 test_% 模式规则（用 $* 取「茎」），依次执行 compile→iverilog→vvp 三步。compile 中 sv2v -I src/* 会吃掉字母序最前的 alu.sv，故 alu 须经 compile_% 规则单独编译、再 cat 拼回 build/gpu.v 并在顶部补 timescale；iverilog 用 -s gpu 指定顶层模块。cocotb 靠 libcocotbvpi_icarus 与 LIBPYTHON_LOC 搭起 Python↔Verilog 桥。测试台 setup.py 启动序列为建时钟、复位、装程序与数据内存、写设备控制寄存器（设 thread_count）、拉 start，主循环用 RisingEdge(dut.clk) 逐拍同步、每拍驱动一次外部内存。日志写入 test/logs/log_<时间戳>.txt，分「初始数据内存」「执行轨迹」「最终数据内存」三段，内存表标题为 DATA MEMORY。引入的关键术语：仿真器、testbench、VPI、模式规则、DCR、start/done。
### u2-l1 gpu.sv 顶层架构

本讲义只拆解 tiny-gpu 的顶层模块 `gpu.sv` 的「连线」，不进入任何子模块内部。核心结论有四点：第一，顶层用 8 个 `parameter` 把数据内存规格（8 位地址/8 位数据/4 通道）、程序内存规格（8 位地址/16 位指令/1 通道）、`NUM_CORES`、`THREADS_PER_BLOCK` 全部参数化，并用 `localparam` 派生出 `NUM_LSUS = NUM_CORES × THREADS_PER_BLOCK` 与 `NUM_FETCHERS = NUM_CORES`。第二，顶层端口分四类：`clk/reset`、内核生命周期握手 `start/done`、DCR 写入接口、以及两套多通道 `valid/ready/data` 内存握手接口（程序内存只读、数据内存可读写）。第三，顶层实例化 4 类子模块：`dcr`（产出 thread_count）、两个 `controller`（数据控制器接 8 个 LSU/4 通道、程序控制器接 2 个 fetcher/1 通道且 `WRITE_ENABLE=0`）、`dispatch`（派发 block 并汇总 done）。第四，`NUM_CORES` 个 core 由 `generate for` 展开；为兼容 Verilog 2005 不能切片顶层信号的限制，每核先接本地 `core_lsu_*`，再用 `always @(posedge clk)` 按 `i*THREADS_PER_BLOCK+j` 重排下标穿透到顶层 `lsu_*` 数组，该寄存器赋值引入 1 拍延迟；fetcher 侧每核仅 1 个，直接对接无需中间寄存器。引入并供后续讲义承接的关键术语：parameter/localparam 参数化、unpackaged 多通道数组端口、`consumer_*`/`mem_*`/`lsu_*`/`fetcher_*` 命名约定、generate 多核展开、LSU/fetcher 穿透寄存器及其延迟。
### u2-l2 内核启动：DCR 与 Dispatcher

本讲解析内核启动的最小模块 DCR（dcr.sv）与 Dispatcher（dispatch.sv），由顶层 gpu.sv 串接。DCR 是一个 8 位寄存器，主机经 write_enable + data 写入 thread_count（非阻塞赋值，下一拍才生效），设定本次内核线程数。Dispatcher 按向上取整式 total_blocks = (thread_count + TPB - 1) / TPB 把线程切成 block，每拍执行「派发 + 回收」两个循环：向 core_reset=1 的空闲核派发 block，并回收 core_start && core_done 的核以复用。关键术语包括：thread_count、THREADS_PER_BLOCK（TPB）、block、total_blocks、core_reset/core_start/core_done 握手信号，以及 blocks_dispatched / blocks_done 计数器。核心结论：派发用阻塞赋值使一拍内能向多核依次派不同 block，控制信号用非阻塞故下一拍才对 core 生效；最后一块走尾数分支 thread_count - blocks_dispatched*TPB；done 在所有 block 收回、blocks_done==total_blocks 命中后下一拍才拉高。core_done 源自 core 内 scheduler 跑到 RET 指令，其内部状态机细节留待后续讲义展开。
### u3-l1 内存模型与外部接口

本讲确立 tiny-gpu 与外部内存的边界约定。设有两块独立内存：data 内存（8 位地址、8 位数据、4 通道，可读写）与 program 内存（8 位地址、16 位指令、1 通道，只读），规格全部由 gpu.sv 的 parameter 定义。对外采用统一的「多通道 valid/ready/data」握手：请求类信号（valid/address/write-data）为 GPU 输出，应答类信号（ready/read-data）为 GPU 输入。两块内存各由一个 controller 实例作中继——data 控制器在 8 个 LSU 与 4 个外部通道间仲裁，program 控制器服务 2 个 fetcher、1 通道且 WRITE_ENABLE=0。仿真中外部内存由 Python 的 Memory 类扮演，每拍 run() 一次、零延迟同拍响应；因 cocotb 将多通道信号序列化为拼接长串，run() 须逐位/逐段解析请求，再以同一布局把应答拼回写回 DUT。load() 灌入初始数据、display() 打印内存表格以供观察。controller 内部仲裁逻辑留待 u3-l2。
### u3-l2 内存控制器：带宽节流

本讲拆解 tiny-gpu 内存控制器 `controller.sv`。它存在的根本原因是带宽瓶颈：消费者（data 控制器 8 个 LSU、program 控制器 2 个 fetcher）多于外部通道（4 条、1 条），均 2 倍过订阅，需一个仲裁中继者把 N 路请求节流到 M 条通道。每条通道独立跑一份五态状态机 `IDLE/READ_WAITING/WRITE_WAITING/READ_RELAYING/WRITE_RELAYING`，由外层 `for i` 并发驱动；`IDLE` 按消费者编号做固定优先级轮询，配 `break` 保证「一通道一周期一请求」。关键术语包括规模参数 `NUM_CONSUMERS/NUM_CHANNELS/WRITE_ENABLE`；跨通道去重锁 `channel_serving_consumer` 的置位/复位用阻塞赋值 `=` 使「领走/释放」同周期内即时可见，而数据通路用非阻塞 `<=` 保持同步时序，体现「协调用阻塞、数据用非阻塞」的混合用法；`current_consumer[i]` 作回执地址，把外部应答精确扔回当初的消费者，读回传数据、写只回确认。核心结论：中继时序上 `WAITING` 等的是外部内存（零延迟约 1 拍），`RELAYING` 等的是消费者撤回 valid（约 2 拍）。本讲只聚焦控制器本身，不涉及 LSU/fetcher 内部状态机及缓存合并等优化。
### u4-l1 Core 解剖结构

本讲只拆解 `core.sv` 一个文件的内部连线，确立 core「一次处理一个 block」的工作模型：dispatcher 派活时递上 `block_id`（映射为 `%blockIdx`）和 `thread_count` 两项 block 元数据。core 内部由三类部件构成：一是**单实例三剑客**——fetcher（取指）、decoder（译码）、scheduler（驱动 `core_state` 七阶段状态机 IDLE→FETCH→DECODE→REQUEST→WAIT→EXECUTE→UPDATE→DONE），它们对应「单指令流」，产出的控制信号（`core_state`、`instruction`、`decoded_*`）被全 core 广播共享；二是**每线程一份**的 ALU/LSU/registers（16 个寄存器，`%threadIdx` 复位为线程号 i）/PC，由 `generate for` 在编译期复制 `THREADS_PER_BLOCK` 套，对应「多数据」。硬件虽建满最大容量，但运行时用 `enable = (i < thread_count)` 门控冻结多余执行单元。两类部件由中间信号缝合：`rs[i]/rt[i]`（registers→ALU/LSU）、`alu_out[i]`（ALU→registers/PC）、`lsu_out[i]`（LSU→registers），在 `core_state` 调度下分 REQUEST/EXECUTE/UPDATE 三拍流动，形成每个线程内 registers↔ALU↔LSU 的闭合数据环路。本讲不展开各子模块内部实现，留待后续讲义。
### u4-l2 Scheduler 核心状态机

scheduler 是 tiny-gpu core 的「指挥」，不参与计算与访存，只把执行一条指令切成七阶段状态机（IDLE→FETCH→DECODE→REQUEST→WAIT→EXECUTE→UPDATE→DONE），用 3 位信号 `core_state` 广播给 fetcher / decoder / LSU / ALU / PC，后者各在自己所属节拍工作——这正是 SIMD 单指令流驱动多线程的硬件体现。其工作粒度是一个 block，从 PC=0 跑到 RET 为止。两类阶段判然分明：DECODE / REQUEST / EXECUTE / UPDATE 是单周期同步推进，根源是非阻塞赋值 `<=` 引入的 1 拍延迟，对所有指令一视同仁；FETCH 与 WAIT 则是变长握手等待。FETCH 靠 `fetcher_state==FETCHED` 与 fetcher 做双向握手；WAIT 用 `for`+`break` 轮询所有线程的 `lsu_state`，只要任一 LSU 仍处 REQUESTING/WAITING 就继续等，因而成为同步指令（1 拍放行）与异步访存（等最慢线程内存往返）的分水岭。UPDATE 阶段以 `current_pc <= next_pc[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1]` 推进 PC，隐含所有线程 PC 相同的「PC 收敛假设」（忽略分支分歧），遇 RET 则置 `done` 进 DONE。单条指令耗时为 `T_inst = t_FETCH + t_WAIT + 4`，解释了内存密集型内核为何更慢。后续讲义将承接 `core_state` 译码、LSU 四态机、寄存器堆写回以及分支分歧等被简化的话题。
### u4-l3 Fetcher 与 Decoder

本讲聚焦 core 单指令流的取指与译码。fetcher 是 IDLE→FETCHING→FETCHED 三态状态机，经 valid/ready 握手从只读程序内存异步取回当前 PC 处的 16 位指令，在 FETCHING→FETCHED 边界锁存进 instruction 寄存器，且译码期间不清零。指令为 16 位定长编码：[15:12]=opcode、[11:8]=rd、[7:4]=rs、[3:0]=rt，而 nzp([11:9])、imm([7:0]) 复用上述字段，含义由 opcode 决定。decoder 在 DECODE 拍纯组合切字段，并「先清零、后 case 查表」拉高一排 decoded_* 控制信号（写回/算术/访存/比较/跳转各类 mux 与 enable）。核心结论：scheduler 广播的 core_state 充当节拍器，分别选通 fetcher（FETCH 拍）与 decoder（DECODE 拍），使单实例取指译码部件与每线程一份的 ALU/LSU/registers/PC 严格同步，构成 SIMD 的硬件基础；控制信号如何被消费留给后续讲义。
### u5-l1 指令集（ISA）与编码

本讲从「指令本身长什么样」切入，给出 tiny-gpu 指令集架构（ISA）的完整契约。核心模块有四：其一，ISA 仅含 11 条指令，分跳转类（BRnzp、RET）、比较类（CMP）、算术类（ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV）、访存常数类（LDR/STR/CONST）及 NOP，操作码在 decoder.sv 用 localparam 写死，是整份指令集的单一事实来源，属 load-store 架构。其二，指令为 16 位定长，切成 opcode[15:12]/rd[11:8]/rs[7:4]/rt[3:0] 四段；位域可被复用，opcode 决定同一字段作寄存器号还是立即数或 nzp 条件位。其三，16 个寄存器中 R0–R12 自由读写，R13–R15 为只读的 %blockIdx/%blockDim/%threadIdx，由硬件 rd<13 写回保护，是 SIMD 让同一段代码处理不同数据的命脉。其四，BRnzp 是唯一控制流指令，用 [11:9] 作 nzp 掩码、[7:0] 作跳转目标，与 CMP 写入的 NZP 寄存器逐位与来决定是否跳转。format.py 的 format_instruction 则是 decoder 的逆运算，用于反汇编与编码验证。
### u5-l2 ALU 与比较/NZP

本讲深入 `alu.sv`，定位 ALU 在 core 数据通路中的角色：它以 `rs/rt` 为输入、`alu_out` 为单出口，处在 registers→ALU→registers/pc 的闭环中，算术结果写回 `rd`，CMP 结果抄入 NZP 寄存器。核心是两只由 decoder 产生的控制阀门：2 位 `decoded_alu_arithmetic_mux` 在 ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV 间四选一；`decoded_alu_output_mux` 在算术模式与比较模式间切换。CMP 模式下 `alu_out[2:0]` 按 N/Z/P 编码：bit[0]=小于、bit[1]=相等、bit[2]=大于。关键结论是：因 rs/rt 为 8 位无符号数，`rs-rt` 不够减时回绕成大正数，使 N 位结构性地恒为 0，故 CMP 实际只能分辨「相等/不等」，无法判定大小方向。时序上 ALU 受 `enable` 与 `core_state==EXECUTE` 双重门控，输出经 `alu_out_reg` 寄存带来 1 拍延迟，形成「EXECUTE 算、UPDATE 用」的节拍咬合。matmul 的 `CMP+BRn` 计数循环正是靠相等/不等判定工作，「负数回绕」非但不是缺陷，反而是循环正确运行的机制。
### u5-l3 LSU 异步访存

本讲围绕 tiny-gpu 的访存执行单元 LSU（Load-Store Unit，`src/lsu.sv`）展开，核心是讲清为何访存需要独立的状态机。算术指令（ADD/SUB 等）在 `EXECUTE` 一拍内自给自足完成；而 LDR/STR 的数据在 core 外部的 data 内存中，需经 LSU→controller→外部内存→controller→LSU 的链路往返，耗时不确定，故须用 `valid/ready` 握手并靠状态机「记住」未完成的请求。LSU 采用 `IDLE→REQUESTING→WAITING→DONE` 四态 FSM（编码 00/01/10/11），由 scheduler 的 `core_state` 门控：`REQUEST` 触发 `IDLE→REQUESTING`，`UPDATE` 复位 `DONE→IDLE`。LDR（读地址=rs）在 `WAITING` 收到 `mem_read_ready` 时把 `mem_read_data` 锁入 `lsu_out`，于 `UPDATE` 写回 `rd`；STR（写地址=rs、写数据=rt）在 `WAITING` 仅撤 `valid`、不写 `lsu_out`——因数据是流出而非回流。`lsu_out` 因此是 LDR 专用的数据出口。scheduler 在 `WAIT` 阶段逐线程轮询 `lsu_state`，凡仍处 `REQUESTING/WAITING` 即原地等待，从而把变长的访存延迟吸收掉；`mem_read_ready`/`mem_write_ready` 则由 controller 中继外部内存应答返回。本讲引入的关键术语：LSU、`lsu_state` 四态、`lsu_out`、core_state 门控、三方握手（scheduler×LSU×controller），为后续寄存器堆与内存优化讲义承接。
### u5-l4 寄存器堆与程序计数器

本讲拆解每线程的寄存器堆（registers.sv）与程序计数器（pc.sv）。寄存器堆含16个8位寄存器：R0–R12自由读写，R13–R15为只读身份寄存器 %blockIdx/%blockDim/%threadIdx，写回时以地址 <13 做硬件保护；它在 REQUEST 阶段读出源操作数 rs/rt，UPDATE 阶段经 reg_input_mux 三路写回（算术←alu_out、访存←lsu_out、常数←立即数）。%blockIdx 每周期无条件刷新为外部 block_id，以冗余写入换取 dispatcher 切换 block 无需重新复位的简单性。PC 在 EXECUTE 阶段计算 next_pc：默认 PC+1，BRnzp 按 (nzp & decoded_nzp)!=0 决定是否跳到立即数。NZP 是粘性信箱，由 CMP 在 UPDATE 写入、由 BRnzp 在 EXECUTE 读取，因阶段错位而天然完成跨指令的比较-跳转交接。current_pc 全 core 共享（单指令流），next_pc 每线程一份但被 PC 收敛假设统一取末尾线程值。
### u6-l1 cocotb 仿真测试框架

本讲把视角从「硬件内部」转向「测试台如何调度硬件」。cocotb 让 Python 充当 testbench，`.sv` 充当被测设计（DUT），二者经 VPI 桥（`libcocotbvpi_icarus`）通信；测试函数是 async 协程，靠 `await` 一个 trigger 把控制权交还仿真器、与硬件同步节拍。核心是 `setup()` 的五步启动序列：建时钟（用 `start_soon` 把方波分叉到后台）、复位脉冲、`load` 装填内存、写 DCR 锁存 `thread_count`、拉 `start` 点火——凡涉 DUT 寄存器都需 `await RisingEdge`，而 `load` 是纯 Python 操作无需等时钟。重点是主循环 `while dut.done.value != 1` 每拍执行 `run()`→`ReadOnly`→`format_cycle`→`RisingEdge`，对应 cocotb 一个周期内 ReadWrite（可写，`Memory.run()` 在此回送多通道内存应答）与 ReadOnly（只读，`format_cycle` 读快照）两阶段，顺序不可颠倒。`Memory` 类以 Python 列表扮演外部 DRAM，每拍零延迟同拍响应；循环退出后由 `assert` 判定成败，轨迹经 `logger.py` 写入带时间戳的 `test/logs/`。引入术语 DUT、VPI、trigger、ReadWrite/ReadOnly、DCR、done，为 u6-l2 执行轨迹阅读与 u6-l3 编写新内核承接。
### u6-l2 执行轨迹格式化与阅读

本讲承接 u6-l1，讲解 cocotb 仿真执行轨迹（execution trace）如何从 DUT 信号翻译为可读日志，主角为 format.py 与 logger.py。核心结论：所有轨迹只写入带时间戳的日志文件、终端无输出。format_cycle 按「cycle→core→thread→字段」四层遍历，每 core 仅读一次 instruction 供全部线程共享（体现 SIMD 单指令流），用核级、线程级与 thread_id 三重过滤控制日志体量，并以 reg_input_mux 选择性打印即将写回的值。关键术语：format_instruction（decoder 逆运算）、四张状态映射表（镜像硬件 localparam，需双向同步）、format_registers（用 reg_idx=15-i 加 reverse 还原 cocotb 倒序遍历的寄存器升序）。字段分 core 共享（PC/Core State/Instruction/Fetcher State）与每线程（Registers/LSU State/RS/RT）两组，是 SIMD 架构的文本投影。两处陷阱：BRnzp 的 nzp 段因字符串与整数比较恒空；format_memory_controller_state 虽定义却从未被调用，属死代码。
### u6-l3 编写与仿真内核

本讲是 Unit 6 的应用篇，承接 u6-l1（驱动硬件）与 u6-l2（读轨迹），讲解如何往 tiny-gpu 塞入自写内核并验证。核心结论：跑内核需备齐「三要素」——程序内存（手工编码的 16 位指令列表）、数据内存（初始数据列表）、线程数（写入 DCR）；README 里的 `.threads`/`.data` 伪指令只供人读，真正生效的是 `test_*.py` 中的 Python 列表，项目并无汇编器。`matadd` 内核演示了 SIMD 主线：用只读寄存器 `%blockIdx/%blockDim/%threadIdx` 算出全局线程号 `i`，按 `baseA/baseB/baseC` 三段布局定位数据，用 `LDR rd,rs`（取 mem[rs] 写 rd）读、`STR rs,rt`（把 rt 写入 mem[rs]，地址/数据字段方向与 LDR 相反）写。`matmul` 内核首次引入循环控制：`CMP`+`BRn` 实现累加循环；关键反直觉点是，因 8 位无符号减法回绕，`CMP` 的 bit[2] 实际等价于「不相等」，`BRn`（掩码 `100`）据此在 `k≠N` 时跳回，行为上等价于「k<N 则循环」，`k==N` 退出。该内核所有线程分支均收敛，满足 scheduler 的「PC 收敛假设」（为 u7-l1 讨论分支分歧埋下伏笔）。校验环节：数据内存分段使输入/输出区不重叠，仿真后用 `data_memory.memory[i+baseC]` 取回结果，与 Python 独立重算的期望值 `assert` 比对；`display` 只写日志供人看，`assert` 才决定成败。写新内核固定五步：设计汇编→手工编码→填 `test_*.py` 三要素→`setup`+主循环→`assert` 校验。

2	`timescale 1ns/1ns

4	// SCHEDULER
5	// > Manages the entire control flow of a single compute core processing 1 block
6	// 1. FETCH - Retrieve instruction at current program counter (PC) from program memory
7	// 2. DECODE - Decode the instruction into the relevant control signals
8	// 3. REQUEST - If we have an instruction that accesses memory, trigger the async memory requests from LSUs
9	// 4. WAIT - Wait for all async memory requests to resolve (if applicable)
10	// 5. EXECUTE - Execute computations on retrieved data from registers / memory
11	// 6. UPDATE - Update register values (including NZP register) and program counter
12	// > Each core has it's own scheduler where multiple threads can be processed with
13	//   the same control flow at once.
14	// > Technically, different instructions can branch to different PCs, requiring "branch divergence." In
15	//   this minimal implementation, we assume no branch divergence (naive approach for simplicity)
16	module scheduler #(
17	    parameter THREADS_PER_BLOCK = 4,
18	) (
19	    input wire clk,
20	    input wire reset,
21	    input wire start,
22	    
23	    // Control Signals
24	    input reg decoded_mem_read_enable,
25	    input reg decoded_mem_write_enable,
26	    input reg decoded_ret,
27	
28	    // Memory Access State
29	    input reg [2:0] fetcher_state,
30	    input reg [1:0] lsu_state [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0],
31	
32	    // Current & Next PC
33	    output reg [7:0] current_pc,
34	    input reg [7:0] next_pc [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0],
35	
36	    // Execution State
37	    output reg [2:0] core_state,
38	    output reg done
39	);
40	    localparam IDLE = 3'b000, // Waiting to start
41	        FETCH = 3'b001,       // Fetch instructions from program memory
42	        DECODE = 3'b010,      // Decode instructions into control signals
43	        REQUEST = 3'b011,     // Request data from registers or memory
44	        WAIT = 3'b100,        // Wait for response from memory if necessary
45	        EXECUTE = 3'b101,     // Execute ALU and PC calculations
46	        UPDATE = 3'b110,      // Update registers, NZP, and PC
47	        DONE = 3'b111;        // Done executing this block
48	    
49	    always @(posedge clk) begin 
50	        if (reset) begin
51	            current_pc <= 0;
52	            core_state <= IDLE;
53	            done <= 0;
54	        end else begin 
55	            case (core_state)
56	                IDLE: begin
57	                    // Here after reset (before kernel is launched, or after previous block has been processed)
58	                    if (start) begin 
59	                        // Start by fetching the next instruction for this block based on PC
60	                        core_state <= FETCH;
61	                    end
62	                end
63	                FETCH: begin 
64	                    // Move on once fetcher_state = FETCHED
65	                    if (fetcher_state == 3'b010) begin 
66	                        core_state <= DECODE;
67	                    end
68	                end
69	                DECODE: begin
70	                    // Decode is synchronous so we move on after one cycle
71	                    core_state <= REQUEST;
72	                end
73	                REQUEST: begin 
74	                    // Request is synchronous so we move on after one cycle
75	                    core_state <= WAIT;
76	                end
77	                WAIT: begin
78	                    // Wait for all LSUs to finish their request before continuing
79	                    reg any_lsu_waiting = 1'b0;
80	                    for (int i = 0; i < THREADS_PER_BLOCK; i++) begin
81	                        // Make sure no lsu_state = REQUESTING or WAITING
82	                        if (lsu_state[i] == 2'b01 || lsu_state[i] == 2'b10) begin
83	                            any_lsu_waiting = 1'b1;
84	                            break;
85	                        end
86	                    end
87	
88	                    // If no LSU is waiting for a response, move onto the next stage
89	                    if (!any_lsu_waiting) begin
90	                        core_state <= EXECUTE;
91	                    end
92	                end
93	                EXECUTE: begin
94	                    // Execute is synchronous so we move on after one cycle
95	                    core_state <= UPDATE;
96	                end
97	                UPDATE: begin 
98	                    if (decoded_ret) begin 
99	                        // If we reach a RET instruction, this block is done executing
100	                        done <= 1;
101	                        core_state <= DONE;
102	                    end else begin 
103	                        // TODO: Branch divergence. For now assume all next_pc converge
104	                        current_pc <= next_pc[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1];
105	
106	                        // Update is synchronous so we move on after one cycle
107	                        core_state <= FETCH;
108	                    end
109	                end
110	                DONE: begin 
111	                    // no-op
112	                end
113	            endcase
114	        end
115	    end
116	endmodule

`default_nettype none
`timescale 1ns/1ns

// COMPUTE CORE
// > Handles processing 1 block at a time
// > The core also has it's own scheduler to manage control flow
// > Each core contains 1 fetcher & decoder, and register files, ALUs, LSUs, PC for each thread
module core #(
    parameter DATA_MEM_ADDR_BITS = 8,
    parameter DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS = 8,
    parameter PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS = 8,
    parameter PROGRAM_MEM_DATA_BITS = 16,
    parameter THREADS_PER_BLOCK = 4
) (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,

    // Kernel Execution
    input wire start,
    output wire done,

    // Block Metadata
    input wire [7:0] block_id,
    input wire [$clog2(THREADS_PER_BLOCK):0] thread_count,

    // Program Memory
    output reg program_mem_read_valid,
    output reg [PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS-1:0] program_mem_read_address,
    input reg program_mem_read_ready,
    input reg [PROGRAM_MEM_DATA_BITS-1:0] program_mem_read_data,

    // Data Memory
    output reg [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0] data_mem_read_valid,
    output reg [DATA_MEM_ADDR_BITS-1:0] data_mem_read_address [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0],
    input reg [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0] data_mem_read_ready,
    input reg [DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS-1:0] data_mem_read_data [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0],
    output reg [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0] data_mem_write_valid,
    output reg [DATA_MEM_ADDR_BITS-1:0] data_mem_write_address [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0],
    output reg [DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS-1:0] data_mem_write_data [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0],
    input reg [THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0] data_mem_write_ready
);
    // State
    reg [2:0] core_state;
    reg [2:0] fetcher_state;
    reg [15:0] instruction;

    // Intermediate Signals
    reg [7:0] current_pc;
    wire [7:0] next_pc[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0];
    reg [7:0] rs[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0];
    reg [7:0] rt[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0];
    reg [1:0] lsu_state[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0];
    reg [7:0] lsu_out[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0];
    wire [7:0] alu_out[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1:0];
    
    // Decoded Instruction Signals
    reg [3:0] decoded_rd_address;
    reg [3:0] decoded_rs_address;
    reg [3:0] decoded_rt_address;
    reg [2:0] decoded_nzp;
    reg [7:0] decoded_immediate;

    // Decoded Control Signals
    reg decoded_reg_write_enable;           // Enable writing to a register
    reg decoded_mem_read_enable;            // Enable reading from memory
    reg decoded_mem_write_enable;           // Enable writing to memory
    reg decoded_nzp_write_enable;           // Enable writing to NZP register
    reg [1:0] decoded_reg_input_mux;        // Select input to register
    reg [1:0] decoded_alu_arithmetic_mux;   // Select arithmetic operation
    reg decoded_alu_output_mux;             // Select operation in ALU
    reg decoded_pc_mux;                     // Select source of next PC
    reg decoded_ret;

    // Fetcher
    fetcher #(
        .PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS(PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS),
        .PROGRAM_MEM_DATA_BITS(PROGRAM_MEM_DATA_BITS)
    ) fetcher_instance (
        .clk(clk),
        .reset(reset),
        .core_state(core_state),
        .current_pc(current_pc),
        .mem_read_valid(program_mem_read_valid),
        .mem_read_address(program_mem_read_address),
        .mem_read_ready(program_mem_read_ready),
        .mem_read_data(program_mem_read_data),
        .fetcher_state(fetcher_state),
        .instruction(instruction) 
    );

    // Decoder
    decoder decoder_instance (
        .clk(clk),
        .reset(reset),
        .core_state(core_state),
        .instruction(instruction),
        .decoded_rd_address(decoded_rd_address),
        .decoded_rs_address(decoded_rs_address),
        .decoded_rt_address(decoded_rt_address),
        .decoded_nzp(decoded_nzp),
        .decoded_immediate(decoded_immediate),
        .decoded_reg_write_enable(decoded_reg_write_enable),
        .decoded_mem_read_enable(decoded_mem_read_enable),
        .decoded_mem_write_enable(decoded_mem_write_enable),
        .decoded_nzp_write_enable(decoded_nzp_write_enable),
        .decoded_reg_input_mux(decoded_reg_input_mux),
        .decoded_alu_arithmetic_mux(decoded_alu_arithmetic_mux),
        .decoded_alu_output_mux(decoded_alu_output_mux),
        .decoded_pc_mux(decoded_pc_mux),
        .decoded_ret(decoded_ret)
    );

    // Scheduler
    scheduler #(
        .THREADS_PER_BLOCK(THREADS_PER_BLOCK),
    ) scheduler_instance (
        .clk(clk),
        .reset(reset),
        .start(start),
        .fetcher_state(fetcher_state),
        .core_state(core_state),
        .decoded_mem_read_enable(decoded_mem_read_enable),
        .decoded_mem_write_enable(decoded_mem_write_enable),
        .decoded_ret(decoded_ret),
        .lsu_state(lsu_state),
        .current_pc(current_pc),
        .next_pc(next_pc),
        .done(done)
    );

    // Dedicated ALU, LSU, registers, & PC unit for each thread this core has capacity for
    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < THREADS_PER_BLOCK; i = i + 1) begin : threads
            // ALU
            alu alu_instance (
                .clk(clk),
                .reset(reset),
                .enable(i < thread_count),
                .core_state(core_state),
                .decoded_alu_arithmetic_mux(decoded_alu_arithmetic_mux),
                .decoded_alu_output_mux(decoded_alu_output_mux),
                .rs(rs[i]),
                .rt(rt[i]),
                .alu_out(alu_out[i])
            );

            // LSU
            lsu lsu_instance (
                .clk(clk),
                .reset(reset),
                .enable(i < thread_count),
                .core_state(core_state),
                .decoded_mem_read_enable(decoded_mem_read_enable),
                .decoded_mem_write_enable(decoded_mem_write_enable),
                .mem_read_valid(data_mem_read_valid[i]),
                .mem_read_address(data_mem_read_address[i]),
                .mem_read_ready(data_mem_read_ready[i]),
                .mem_read_data(data_mem_read_data[i]),
                .mem_write_valid(data_mem_write_valid[i]),
                .mem_write_address(data_mem_write_address[i]),
                .mem_write_data(data_mem_write_data[i]),
                .mem_write_ready(data_mem_write_ready[i]),
                .rs(rs[i]),
                .rt(rt[i]),
                .lsu_state(lsu_state[i]),
                .lsu_out(lsu_out[i])
            );

            // Register File
            registers #(
                .THREADS_PER_BLOCK(THREADS_PER_BLOCK),
                .THREAD_ID(i),
                .DATA_BITS(DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS),
            ) register_instance (
                .clk(clk),
                .reset(reset),
                .enable(i < thread_count),
                .block_id(block_id),
                .core_state(core_state),
                .decoded_reg_write_enable(decoded_reg_write_enable),
                .decoded_reg_input_mux(decoded_reg_input_mux),
                .decoded_rd_address(decoded_rd_address),
                .decoded_rs_address(decoded_rs_address),
                .decoded_rt_address(decoded_rt_address),
                .decoded_immediate(decoded_immediate),
                .alu_out(alu_out[i]),
                .lsu_out(lsu_out[i]),
                .rs(rs[i]),
                .rt(rt[i])
            );

            // Program Counter
            pc #(
                .DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS(DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS),
                .PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS(PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS)
            ) pc_instance (
                .clk(clk),
                .reset(reset),
                .enable(i < thread_count),
                .core_state(core_state),
                .decoded_nzp(decoded_nzp),
                .decoded_immediate(decoded_immediate),
                .decoded_nzp_write_enable(decoded_nzp_write_enable),
                .decoded_pc_mux(decoded_pc_mux),
                .alu_out(alu_out[i]),
                .current_pc(current_pc),
                .next_pc(next_pc[i])
            );
        end
    endgenerate

This is challenging since these projects aim at being feature complete and functional, so they're quite complex. 36 37 This is why I built `tiny-gpu`! 38 39 ## What is tiny-gpu? 40 41 > [!IMPORTANT] 42 > 43 > **tiny-gpu** is a minimal GPU implementation optimized for learning about how GPUs work from the ground up. 44 > 45 > Specifically, with the trend toward general-purpose GPUs (GPGPUs) and ML-accelerators like Google's TPU, tiny-gpu focuses on highlighting the general principles of all of these architectures, rather than on the details of graphics-specific hardware. 46 47 With this motivation in mind, we can simplify GPUs by cutting out the majority of complexity involved with building a production-grade graphics card, and focus on the core elements that are critical to all of these modern hardware accelerators. 48 49 This project is primarily focused on exploring: 50 51 1. **Architecture** - What does the architecture of a GPU look like? What are the most important elements? 52 2. **Parallelization** - How is the SIMD progamming model implemented in hardware? 53 3. **Memory** - How does a GPU work around the constraints of limited memory bandwidth? 54 55 After understanding the fundamentals laid out in this project, you can checkout the [advanced functionality section](#advanced-functionality) to understand some of the most important optimizations made in production grade GPUs (that are more challenging to implement) which improve performance. 56 57 # Architecture 58 59

60 61 62

63 64 ## GPU 65 66 tiny-gpu is built to execute a single kernel at a time. 67 68 In order to launch a kernel, we need to do the following: 69 70 1. Load global program memory with the kernel code 71 2. Load data memory with the necessary data 72 3. Specify the number of threads to launch in the device control register 73 4. Launch the kernel by setting the start signal to high. 74 75 The GPU itself consists of the following units: 76 77 1. Device control register 78 2. Dispatcher 79 3. Variable number of compute cores 80 4. Memory controllers for data memory & program memory 81 5. Cache 82 83 ### Device Control Register 84 85 The device control register usually stores metadata specifying how kernels should be executed on the GPU. 86 87 In this case, the device control register just stores the `thread_count` - the total number of threads to launch for the active kernel. 88 89 ### Dispatcher 90 91 Once a kernel is launched, the dispatcher is the unit that actually manages the distribution of threads to different compute cores. 92 93 The dispatcher organizes threads into groups that can be executed in parallel on a single core called **blocks** and sends these blocks off to be processed by available cores. 94 95 Once all blocks have been processed, the dispatcher reports back that the kernel execution is done. 96 97 ## Memory 98 99 The GPU is built to interface with an external global memory. Here, data memory and program memory are separated out for simplicity. 100 101 ### Global Memory 102 103 tiny-gpu data memory has the following specifications: 104 105 - 8 bit addressability (256 total rows of data memory) 106 - 8 bit data (stores values of <256 for each row) 107 108 tiny-gpu program memory has the following specifications: 109 110 - 8 bit addressability (256 rows of program memory) 111 - 16 bit data (each instruction is 16 bits as specified by the ISA) 112 113 ### Memory Controllers 114 115 Global memory has fixed read/write bandwidth, but there may be far more incoming requests across all cores to access data from memory than the external memory is actually able to handle. 116 117 The memory controllers keep track of all the outgoing requests to memory from the compute cores, throttle requests based on actual external memory bandwidth, and relay responses from external memory back to the proper resources. 118 119 Each memory controller has a fixed number of channels based on the bandwidth of global memory. 120 121 ### Cache (WIP) 122 123 The same data is often requested from global memory by multiple cores. Constantly access global memory repeatedly is expensive, and since the data has already been fetched once, it would be more efficient to store it on device in SRAM to be retrieved much quicker on later requests. 124 125 This is exactly what the cache is used for. Data retrieved from external memory is stored in cache and can be retrieved from there on later requests, freeing up memory bandwidth to be used for new data. 126 127 ## Core 128 129 Each core has a number of compute resources, often built around a certain number of threads it can support. In order to maximize parallelization, these resources need to be managed optimally to maximize resource utilization. 130 131 In this simplified GPU, each core processed one **block** at a time, and for each thread in a block, the core has a dedicated ALU, LSU, PC, and register file. Managing the execution of thread instructions on these resources is one of the most challening problems in GPUs. 132 133 ### Scheduler 134 135 Each core has a single scheduler that manages the execution of threads. 136 137 The tiny-gpu scheduler executes instructions for a single block to completion before picking up a new block, and it executes instructions for all threads in-sync and sequentially. 138 139 In more advanced schedulers, techniques like **pipelining** are used to stream the execution of multiple instructions subsequent instructions to maximize resource utilization before previous instructions are fully complete. Additionally, **warp scheduling** can be use to execute multiple batches of threads within a block in parallel. 140 141 The main constraint the scheduler has to work around is the latency associated with loading & storing data from global memory. While most instructions can be executed synchronously, these load-store operations are asynchronous, meaning the rest of the instruction execution has to be built around these long wait times. 142 143 ### Fetcher 144 145 Asynchronously fetches the instruction at the current program counter from program memory (most should actually be fetching from cache after a single block is executed). 146 147 ### Decoder 148 149 Decodes the fetched instruction into control signals for thread execution. 150 151 ### Register Files 152 153 Each thread has it's own dedicated set of register files. The register files hold the data that each thread is performing computations on, which enables the same-instruction multiple-data (SIMD) pattern. 154 155 Importantly, each register file contains a few read-only registers holding data about the current block & thread being executed locally, enabling kernels to be executed with different data based on the local thread id. 156 157 ### ALUs 158 159 Dedicated arithmetic-logic unit for each thread to perform computations. Handles the `ADD`, `SUB`, `MUL`, `DIV` arithmetic instructions. 160 161 Also handles the `CMP` comparison instruction which actually outputs whether the result of the difference between two registers is negative, zero or positive - and stores the result in the `NZP` register in the PC unit. 162 163 ### LSUs 164 165 Dedicated load-store unit for each thread to access global data memory. 166 167 Handles the `LDR` & `STR` instructions - and handles async wait times for memory requests to be processed and relayed by the memory controller. 168 169 ### PCs 170 171 Dedicated program-counter for each unit to determine the next instructions to execute on each thread. 172 173 By default, the PC increments by 1 after every instruction. 174 175 With the `BRnzp` instruction, the NZP register checks to see if the NZP register (set by a previous `CMP` instruction) matches some case - and if it does, it will branch to a specific line of program memory. _This is how loops and conditionals are implemented._ 176 177 Since threads are processed in parallel, tiny-gpu assumes that all threads "converge" to the same program counter after each instruction - which is a naive assumption for the sake of simplicity. 178 179 In real GPUs, individual threads can branch to different PCs, causing **branch divergence** where a group of threads threads initially being processed together has to split out into separate execution. 180 181 # ISA 182 183 ![ISA](/docs/images/isa.png) 184 185 tiny-gpu implements a simple 11 instruction ISA built to enable simple kernels for proof-of-concept like matrix addition & matrix multiplication (implementation further down on this page). 186 187 For these purposes, it supports the following instructions: 188 189 - `BRnzp` - Branch instruction to jump to another line of program memory if the NZP register matches the `nzp` condition in the instruction. 190 - `CMP` - Compare the value of two registers and store the result in the NZP register to use for a later `BRnzp` instruction. 191 - `ADD`, `SUB`, `MUL`, `DIV` - Basic arithmetic operations to enable tensor math. 192 - `LDR` - Load data from global memory. 193 - `STR` - Store data into global memory. 194 - `CONST` - Load a constant value into a register. 195 - `RET` - Signal that the current thread has reached the end of execution. 196 197 Each register is specified by 4 bits, meaning that there are 16 total registers. The first 13 register `R0` - `R12` are free registers that support read/write. The last 3 registers are special read-only registers used to supply the `%blockIdx`, `%blockDim`, and `%threadIdx` critical to SIMD. 198 199 # Execution 200 201 ### Core 202 203 Each core follows the following control flow going through different stages to execute each instruction: 204 205 1. `FETCH` - Fetch the next instruction at current program counter from program memory. 206 2. `DECODE` - Decode the instruction into control signals. 207 3. `REQUEST` - Request data from global memory if necessary (if `LDR` or `STR` instruction). 208 4. `WAIT` - Wait for data from global memory if applicable. 209 5. `EXECUTE` - Execute any computations on data. 210 6. `UPDATE` - Update register files and NZP register. 211 212 The control flow is laid out like this for the sake of simplicity and understandability. 213 214 In practice, several of these steps could be compressed to be optimize processing times, and the GPU could also use **pipelining** to stream and coordinate the execution of many instructions on a cores resources without waiting for previous instructions to finish. 215 216 ### Thread 217 218 ![Thread](/docs/images/thread.png) 219 220 Each thread within each core follows the above execution path to perform computations on the data in it's dedicated register file. 221 222 This resembles a standard CPU diagram, and is quite similar in functionality as well. The main difference is that the `%blockIdx`, `%blockDim`, and `%threadIdx` values lie in the read-only registers for each thread, enabling SIMD functionality. 223 224 # Kernels 225 226 I wrote a matrix addition and matrix multiplication kernel using my ISA as a proof of concept to demonstrate SIMD programming and execution with my GPU. The test files in this repository are capable of fully simulating the execution of these kernels on the GPU, producing data memory states and a complete execution trace. 227 228 ### Matrix Addition 229 230 This matrix addition kernel adds two 1 x 8 matrices by performing 8 element wise additions in separate threads. 231 232 This demonstration makes use of the `%blockIdx`, `%blockDim`, and `%threadIdx` registers to show SIMD programming on this GPU. It also uses the `LDR` and `STR` instructions which require async memory management. 233 234 `matadd.asm` 235 236 ```asm 237 .threads 8 238 .data 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 ; matrix A (1 x 8) 239 .data 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 ; matrix B (1 x 8) 240 241 MUL R0, %blockIdx, %blockDim 242 ADD R0, R0, %threadIdx ; i = blockIdx * blockDim + threadIdx 243 244 CONST R1, #0 ; baseA (matrix A base address) 245 CONST R2, #8 ; baseB (matrix B base address) 246 CONST R3, #16 ; baseC (matrix C base address) 247 248 ADD R4, R1, R0 ; addr(A[i]) = baseA + i 249 LDR R4, R4 ; load A[i] from global memory 250 251 ADD R5, R2, R0 ; addr(B[i]) = baseB + i 252 LDR R5, R5 ; load B[i] from global memory 253 254 ADD R6, R4, R5 ; C[i] = A[i] + B[i] 255 256 ADD R7, R3, R0 ; addr(C[i]) = baseC + i 257 STR R7, R6 ; store C[i] in global memory 258 259 RET ; end of kernel 260 ``` 261 262 ### Matrix Multiplication 263 264 The matrix multiplication kernel multiplies two 2x2 matrices. It performs element wise calculation of the dot product of the relevant row and column and uses the `CMP` and `BRnzp` instructions to demonstrate branching within the threads (notably, all branches converge so this kernel works on the current tiny-gpu implementation). 265 266 `matmul.asm` 267 268 ```asm 269 .threads 4 270 .data 1 2 3 4 ; matrix A (2 x 2) 271 .data 1 2 3 4 ; matrix B (2 x 2) 272 273 MUL R0, %blockIdx, %blockDim 274 ADD R0, R0, %threadIdx ; i = blockIdx * blockDim + threadIdx 275 276 CONST R1, #1 ; increment 277 CONST R2, #2 ; N (matrix inner dimension) 278 CONST R3, #0 ; baseA (matrix A base address) 279 CONST R4, #4 ; baseB (matrix B base address) 280 CONST R5, #8 ; baseC (matrix C base address) 281 282 DIV R6, R0, R2 ; row = i // N 283 MUL R7, R6, R2 284 SUB R7, R0, R7 ; col = i % N 285 286 CONST R8, #0 ; acc = 0 287 CONST R9, #0 ; k = 0 288 289 LOOP: 290 MUL R10, R6, R2 291 ADD R10, R10, R9 292 ADD R10, R10, R3 ; addr(A[i]) = row * N + k + baseA 293 LDR R10, R10 ; load A[i] from global memory 294 295 MUL R11, R9, R2 296 ADD R11, R11, R7 297 ADD R11, R11, R4 ; addr(B[i]) = k * N + col + baseB 298 LDR R11, R11 ; load B[i] from global memory 299 300 MUL R12, R10, R11 301 ADD R8, R8, R12 ; acc = acc + A[i] * B[i] 302 303 ADD R9, R9, R1 ; increment k 304 305 CMP R9, R2 306 BRn LOOP ; loop while k < N 307 308 ADD R9, R5, R0 ; addr(C[i]) = baseC + i 309 STR R9, R8 ; store C[i] in global memory 310 311 RET ; end of kernel 312 ``` 313 314 # Simulation 315 316 tiny-gpu is setup to simulate the execution of both of the above kernels. Before simulating, you'll need to install [iverilog](https://steveicarus.github.io/iverilog/usage/installation.html) and [cocotb](https://docs.cocotb.org/en/stable/install.html): 317 318 - Install Verilog compilers with `brew install icarus-verilog` and `pip3 install cocotb` 319 - Download the latest version of sv2v from https://github.com/zachjs/sv2v/releases, unzip it and put the binary in $PATH. 320 - Run `mkdir build` in the root directory of this repository. 321 322 Once you've installed the pre-requisites, you can run the kernel simulations with `make test_matadd` and `make test_matmul`. 323 324 Executing the simulations will output a log file in `test/logs` with the initial data memory state, complete execution trace of the kernel, and final data memory state. 325 326 If you look at the initial data memory state logged at the start of the logfile for each, you should see the two start matrices for the calculation, and in the final data memory at the end of the file you should also see the resultant matrix. 327 328 Below is a sample of the execution traces, showing on each cycle the execution of every thread within every core, including the current instruction, PC, register values, states, etc. 329 330 ![execution trace](docs/images/trace.png) 331 332 **For anyone trying to run the simulation or play with this repo, please feel free to DM me on [twitter](https://twitter.com/majmudaradam) if you run into any issues - I want you to get this running!** 333 334 # Advanced Functionality 335 336 For the sake of simplicity, there were many additional features implemented in modern GPUs that heavily improve performance & functionality that tiny-gpu omits. We'll discuss some of those most critical features in this section. 337 338 ### Multi-layered Cache & Shared Memory 339 340 In modern GPUs, multiple different levels of caches are used to minimize the amount of data that needs to get accessed from global memory. tiny-gpu implements only one cache layer between individual compute units requesting memory and the memory controllers which stores recent cached data. 341 342 Implementing multi-layered caches allows frequently accessed data to be cached more locally to where it's being used (with some caches within individual compute cores), minimizing load times for this data. 343 344 Different caching algorithms are used to maximize cache-hits - this is a critical dimension that can be improved on to optimize memory access. 345 346 Additionally, GPUs often use **shared memory** for threads within the same block to access a single memory space that can be used to share results with other threads. 347 348 ### Memory Coalescing 349 350 Another critical memory optimization used by GPUs is **memory coalescing.** Multiple threads running in parallel often need to access sequential addresses in memory (for example, a group of threads accessing neighboring elements in a matrix) - but each of these memory requests is put in separately. 351 352 Memory coalescing is used to analyzing queued memory requests and combine neighboring requests into a single transaction, minimizing time spent on addressing, and making all the requests together. 353 354 ### Pipelining 355 356 In the control flow for tiny-gpu, cores wait for one instruction to be executed on a group of threads before starting execution of the next instruction. 357 358 Modern GPUs use **pipelining** to stream execution of multiple sequential instructions at once while ensuring that instructions with dependencies on each other still get executed sequentially. 359 360 This helps to maximize resource utilization within cores as resources are not sitting idle while waiting (ex: during async memory requests). 361 362 ### Warp Scheduling 363 364 Another strategy used to maximize resource utilization on course is **warp scheduling.** This approach involves breaking up blocks into individual batches of theads that can be executed together. 365 366 Multiple warps can be executed on a single core simultaneously by executing instructions from one warp while another warp is waiting. This is similar to pipelining, but dealing with instructions from different threads. 367 368 ### Branch Divergence 369 370 tiny-gpu assumes that all threads in a single batch end up on the same PC after each instruction, meaning that threads can be executed in parallel for their entire lifetime. 371 372 In reality, individual threads could diverge from each other and branch to different lines based on their data. With different PCs, these threads would need to split into separate lines of execution, which requires managing diverging threads & paying attention to when threads converge again. 373 374 ### Synchronization & Barriers 375 376 Another core functionality of modern GPUs is the ability to set **barriers** so that groups of threads in a block can synchronize and wait until all other threads in the same block have gotten to a certain point before continuing execution. 377 378 This is useful for cases where threads need to exchange shared data with each other so they can ensure that the data has been fully processed. 379 380 # Next Steps 381 382 Updates I want to make in the future to improve the design, anyone else is welcome to contribute as well: 383 384 - [ ] Add a simple cache for instructions 385 - [ ] Build an adapter to use GPU with Tiny Tapeout 7 386 - [ ] Add basic branch divergence 387 - [ ] Add basic memory coalescing 388 - [ ] Add basic pipelining 389 - [ ] Optimize control flow and use of registers to improve cycle time 390 - [ ] Write a basic graphics kernel or add simple graphics hardware to demonstrate graphics functionality 391 392 **For anyone curious to play around or make a contribution, feel free to put up a PR with any improvements you'd like to add 😄** 393

This demonstration makes use of the `%blockIdx`, `%blockDim`, and `%threadIdx` registers to show SIMD programming on this GPU. It also uses the `LDR` and `STR` instructions which require async memory management. `matadd.asm` ```asm .threads 8 .data 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 ; matrix A (1 x 8) .data 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 ; matrix B (1 x 8) MUL R0, %blockIdx, %blockDim ADD R0, R0, %threadIdx ; i = blockIdx * blockDim + threadIdx CONST R1, #0 ; baseA (matrix A base address) CONST R2, #8 ; baseB (matrix B base address) CONST R3, #16 ; baseC (matrix C base address) ADD R4, R1, R0 ; addr(A[i]) = baseA + i LDR R4, R4 ; load A[i] from global memory ADD R5, R2, R0 ; addr(B[i]) = baseB + i LDR R5, R5 ; load B[i] from global memory ADD R6, R4, R5 ; C[i] = A[i] + B[i] ADD R7, R3, R0 ; addr(C[i]) = baseC + i STR R7, R6 ; store C[i] in global memory RET ; end of kernel ``` ### Matrix Multiplication The matrix multiplication kernel multiplies two 2x2 matrices. It performs element wise calculation of the dot product of the relevant row and column and uses the `CMP` and `BRnzp` instructions to demonstrate branching within the threads (notably, all branches converge so this kernel works on the current tiny-gpu implementation). `matmul.asm` ```asm .threads 4 .data 1 2 3 4 ; matrix A (2 x 2) .data 1 2 3 4 ; matrix B (2 x 2) MUL R0, %blockIdx, %blockDim ADD R0, R0, %threadIdx ; i = blockIdx * blockDim + threadIdx CONST R1, #1 ; increment CONST R2, #2 ; N (matrix inner dimension) CONST R3, #0 ; baseA (matrix A base address) CONST R4, #4 ; baseB (matrix B base address) CONST R5, #8 ; baseC (matrix C base address) DIV R6, R0, R2 ; row = i // N MUL R7, R6, R2 SUB R7, R0, R7 ; col = i % N CONST R8, #0 ; acc = 0 CONST R9, #0 ; k = 0 LOOP: MUL R10, R6, R2 ADD R10, R10, R9 ADD R10, R10, R3 ; addr(A[i]) = row * N + k + baseA LDR R10, R10 ; load A[i] from global memory MUL R11, R9, R2 ADD R11, R11, R7 ADD R11, R11, R4 ; addr(B[i]) = k * N + col + baseB LDR R11, R11 ; load B[i] from global memory MUL R12, R10, R11 ADD R8, R8, R12 ; acc = acc + A[i] * B[i] ADD R9, R9, R1 ; increment k CMP R9, R2 BRn LOOP ; loop while k < N ADD R9, R5, R0 ; addr(C[i]) = baseC + i STR R9, R8 ; store C[i] in global memory RET ; end of kernel ``` # Simulation tiny-gpu is setup to simulate the execution of both of the above kernels. Before simulating, you'll need to install [iverilog](https://steveicarus.github.io/iverilog/usage/installation.html) and [cocotb](https://docs.cocotb.org/en/stable/install.html): - Install Verilog compilers with `brew install icarus-verilog` and `pip3 install cocotb` - Download the latest version of sv2v from https://github.com/zachjs/sv2v/releases, unzip it and put the binary in $PATH. - Run `mkdir build` in the root directory of this repository. Once you've installed the pre-requisites, you can run the kernel simulations with `make test_matadd` and `make test_matmul`. Executing the simulations will output a log file in `test/logs` with the initial data memory state, complete execution trace of the kernel, and final data memory state. If you look at the initial data memory state logged at the start of the logfile for each, you should see the two start matrices for the calculation, and in the final data memory at the end of the file you should also see the resultant matrix. Below is a sample of the execution traces, showing on each cycle the execution of every thread within every core, including the current instruction, PC, register values, states, etc. ![execution trace](docs/images/trace.png) **For anyone trying to run the simulation or play with this repo, please feel free to DM me on [twitter](https://twitter.com/majmudaradam) if you run into any issues - I want you to get this running!** # Advanced Functionality For the sake of simplicity, there were many additional features implemented in modern GPUs that heavily improve performance & functionality that tiny-gpu omits. We'll discuss some of those most critical features in this section. ### Multi-layered Cache & Shared Memory In modern GPUs, multiple different levels of caches are used to minimize the amount of data that needs to get accessed from global memory. tiny-gpu implements only one cache layer between individual compute units requesting memory and the memory controllers which stores recent cached data. Implementing multi-layered caches allows frequently accessed data to be cached more locally to where it's being used (with some caches within individual compute cores), minimizing load times for this data. Different caching algorithms are used to maximize cache-hits - this is a critical dimension that can be improved on to optimize memory access. Additionally, GPUs often use **shared memory** for threads within the same block to access a single memory space that can be used to share results with other threads. ### Memory Coalescing Another critical memory optimization used by GPUs is **memory coalescing.** Multiple threads running in parallel often need to access sequential addresses in memory (for example, a group of threads accessing neighboring elements in a matrix) - but each of these memory requests is put in separately. Memory coalescing is used to analyzing queued memory requests and combine neighboring requests into a single transaction, minimizing time spent on addressing, and making all the requests together. ### Pipelining In the control flow for tiny-gpu, cores wait for one instruction to be executed on a group of threads before starting execution of the next instruction. Modern GPUs use **pipelining** to stream execution of multiple sequential instructions at once while ensuring that instructions with dependencies on each other still get executed sequentially. This helps to maximize resource utilization within cores as resources are not sitting idle while waiting (ex: during async memory requests). ### Warp Scheduling Another strategy used to maximize resource utilization on course is **warp scheduling.** This approach involves breaking up blocks into individual batches of theads that can be executed together. Multiple warps can be executed on a single core simultaneously by executing instructions from one warp while another warp is waiting. This is similar to pipelining, but dealing with instructions from different threads. ### Branch Divergence tiny-gpu assumes that all threads in a single batch end up on the same PC after each instruction, meaning that threads can be executed in parallel for their entire lifetime. In reality, individual threads could diverge from each other and branch to different lines based on their data. With different PCs, these threads would need to split into separate lines of execution, which requires managing diverging threads & paying attention to when threads converge again. ### Synchronization & Barriers Another core functionality of modern GPUs is the ability to set **barriers** so that groups of threads in a block can synchronize and wait until all other threads in the same block have gotten to a certain point before continuing execution. This is useful for cases where threads need to exchange shared data with each other so they can ensure that the data has been fully processed. # Next Steps Updates I want to make in the future to improve the design, anyone else is welcome to contribute as well: - [ ] Add a simple cache for instructions - [ ] Build an adapter to use GPU with Tiny Tapeout 7 - [ ] Add basic branch divergence - [ ] Add basic memory coalescing - [ ] Add basic pipelining - [ ] Optimize control flow and use of registers to improve cycle time - [ ] Write a basic graphics kernel or add simple graphics hardware to demonstrate graphics functionality **For anyone curious to play around or make a contribution, feel free to put up a PR with any improvements you'd like to add 😄**

1	`default_nettype none
2	`timescale 1ns/1ns
3	
4	// PROGRAM COUNTER
5	// > Calculates the next PC for each thread to update to (but currently we assume all threads
6	//   update to the same PC and don't support branch divergence)
7	// > Currently, each thread in each core has it's own calculation for next PC
8	// > The NZP register value is set by the CMP instruction (based on >/=/< comparison) to 
9	//   initiate the BRnzp instruction for branching
10	module pc #(
11	    parameter DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS = 8,
12	    parameter PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS = 8
13	) (
14	    input wire clk,
15	    input wire reset,
16	    input wire enable, // If current block has less threads then block size, some PCs will be inactive
17	
18	    // State
19	    input reg [2:0] core_state,
20	
21	    // Control Signals
22	    input reg [2:0] decoded_nzp,
23	    input reg [DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS-1:0] decoded_immediate,
24	    input reg decoded_nzp_write_enable,
25	    input reg decoded_pc_mux, 
26	
27	    // ALU Output - used for alu_out[2:0] to compare with NZP register
28	    input reg [DATA_MEM_DATA_BITS-1:0] alu_out,
29	
30	    // Current & Next PCs
31	    input reg [PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS-1:0] current_pc,
32	    output reg [PROGRAM_MEM_ADDR_BITS-1:0] next_pc
33	);
34	    reg [2:0] nzp;
35	
36	    always @(posedge clk) begin
37	        if (reset) begin
38	            nzp <= 3'b0;
39	            next_pc <= 0;
40	        end else if (enable) begin
41	            // Update PC when core_state = EXECUTE
42	            if (core_state == 3'b101) begin 
43	                if (decoded_pc_mux == 1) begin 
44	                    if (((nzp & decoded_nzp) != 3'b0)) begin 
45	                        // On BRnzp instruction, branch to immediate if NZP case matches previous CMP
46	                        next_pc <= decoded_immediate;
47	                    end else begin 
48	                        // Otherwise, just update to PC + 1 (next line)
49	                        next_pc <= current_pc + 1;
50	                    end
51	                end else begin 
52	                    // By default update to PC + 1 (next line)
53	                    next_pc <= current_pc + 1;
54	                end
55	            end   
56	
57	            // Store NZP when core_state = UPDATE   
58	            if (core_state == 3'b110) begin 
59	                // Write to NZP register on CMP instruction
60	                if (decoded_nzp_write_enable) begin
61	                    nzp[2] <= alu_out[2];
62	                    nzp[1] <= alu_out[1];
63	                    nzp[0] <= alu_out[0];
64	                end
65	            end      
66	        end
67	    end
68	
69	endmodule

1	# Scheduler 核心状态机
2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	学完本讲后，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 画出 `scheduler` 驱动一条指令执行完整生命周期的七阶段状态机。
8	2. 说明 `core_state` 如何被 `scheduler` 产出、又被 core 内的 fetcher / decoder / LSU / ALU / PC 共享消费。
9	3. 解释为什么 `DECODE / REQUEST / EXECUTE / UPDATE` 是「单周期同步推进」，而 `FETCH` 与 `WAIT` 是「变长握手等待」。
10	4. 理解 `WAIT` 阶段为什么要轮询所有线程的 `lsu_state`，以及它如何成为同步指令与异步访存的分水岭。
11	5. 解释 `UPDATE` 阶段里 `current_pc <= next_pc[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1]` 这行代码背后的 **PC 收敛假设**，以及 `RET → DONE` 如何标志一个 block 结束。
12	
13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	在进入源码前，先建立三个直觉。
16	
17	### 2.1 什么是「调度器」
18	
19	在前一讲 [u4-l1](u4-l1-core-anatomy.md) 里，我们把 core 拆成了「单实例三剑客（fetcher / decoder / scheduler）」+「每线程一份（ALU / LSU / registers / PC）」两大类部件。其中 **scheduler 就是整个 core 的「指挥」**：它不计算数据，也不读写内存，它的唯一职责是决定「现在该让哪个部件干活」。
20	
21	scheduler 把这个决定编码成一个 3 位信号 `core_state` 广播给全 core。core 里的每个子模块都盯着 `core_state`，只在属于自己的那一拍里工作。理解了 scheduler，就理解了 core 的「心跳节拍」。
22	
23	### 2.2 非阻塞赋值与时钟节拍（关键）
24	
25	本讲要频繁判断「某阶段占几个周期」。tiny-gpu 全部用同一时钟 `clk`，并且 `scheduler` 内部一律使用 **非阻塞赋值 `<=`**。它的后果是：
26	
27	> 在第 N 个上升沿写下的 `core_state <= FETCH`，要到第 N+1 个上升沿才被别的模块「看见」。
28	
29	因此「scheduler 决定进入 FETCH」和「fetcher 真的开始干活」之间天然隔 1 拍。这就是为什么状态机里大量阶段注释写着 *"synchronous so we move on after one cycle"*——它们各自固定占 1 拍，根源正是非阻塞赋值引入的 1 拍延迟。如果你对 `<=` 与 `=` 的区别还不熟，可以回头参考 [u2-l2](u2-l2-kernel-launch-dcr-dispatcher.md) 与 [u3-l2](u3-l2-memory-controller.md) 的对比说明。
30	
31	### 2.3 同步指令 vs 异步访存
32	
33	tiny-gpu 的 11 条指令里，绝大多数（ADD / SUB / MUL / DIV / CMP / CONST / BRnzp / NOP）是 **同步指令**——数据已经躺在寄存器里，ALU 一拍就能算完。只有 LDR / STR 是 **异步访存**——它们要请 LSU 去外部 data 内存取/存数据，而外部内存经由 controller 中继、响应时间不固定（详见 [u3-l2](u3-l2-memory-controller.md)）。
34	
35	scheduler 的状态机之所以专门设计一个 `WAIT` 阶段，就是为了把「等不等内存」这件事统一抽象出来：是同步指令就 1 拍走过，是异步访存就一直等到所有 LSU 都收到应答为止。
36	
37	## 3. 本讲源码地图
38	
39	| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
40	| --- | --- | --- |
41	| [src/scheduler.sv](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/src/scheduler.sv) | core 的控制流状态机 | **本讲主角**：七阶段定义与每个阶段的转移条件 |
42	| [src/core.sv](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/src/core.sv) | 计算核心 | scheduler 如何被实例化、`core_state` 如何广播给各子模块 |

# Scheduler 核心状态机

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲后，你应该能够：

1. 画出 `scheduler` 驱动一条指令执行完整生命周期的七阶段状态机。
2. 说明 `core_state` 如何被 `scheduler` 产出、又被 core 内的 fetcher / decoder / LSU / ALU / PC 共享消费。
3. 解释为什么 `DECODE / REQUEST / EXECUTE / UPDATE` 是「单周期同步推进」，而 `FETCH` 与 `WAIT` 是「变长握手等待」。
4. 理解 `WAIT` 阶段为什么要轮询所有线程的 `lsu_state`，以及它如何成为同步指令与异步访存的分水岭。
5. 解释 `UPDATE` 阶段里 `current_pc <= next_pc[THREADS_PER_BLOCK-1]` 这行代码背后的 **PC 收敛假设**，以及 `RET → DONE` 如何标志一个 block 结束。

## 2. 前置知识

在进入源码前，先建立三个直觉。

### 2.1 什么是「调度器」

在前一讲 [u4-l1](u4-l1-core-anatomy.md) 里，我们把 core 拆成了「单实例三剑客（fetcher / decoder / scheduler）」+「每线程一份（ALU / LSU / registers / PC）」两大类部件。其中 **scheduler 就是整个 core 的「指挥」**：它不计算数据，也不读写内存，它的唯一职责是决定「现在该让哪个部件干活」。

scheduler 把这个决定编码成一个 3 位信号 `core_state` 广播给全 core。core 里的每个子模块都盯着 `core_state`，只在属于自己的那一拍里工作。理解了 scheduler，就理解了 core 的「心跳节拍」。

### 2.2 非阻塞赋值与时钟节拍（关键）

本讲要频繁判断「某阶段占几个周期」。tiny-gpu 全部用同一时钟 `clk`，并且 `scheduler` 内部一律使用 **非阻塞赋值 `<=`**。它的后果是：

> 在第 N 个上升沿写下的 `core_state <= FETCH`，要到第 N+1 个上升沿才被别的模块「看见」。

因此「scheduler 决定进入 FETCH」和「fetcher 真的开始干活」之间天然隔 1 拍。这就是为什么状态机里大量阶段注释写着 *"synchronous so we move on after one cycle"*——它们各自固定占 1 拍，根源正是非阻塞赋值引入的 1 拍延迟。如果你对 `<=` 与 `=` 的区别还不熟，可以回头参考 [u2-l2](u2-l2-kernel-launch-dcr-dispatcher.md) 与 [u3-l2](u3-l2-memory-controller.md) 的对比说明。

### 2.3 同步指令 vs 异步访存

tiny-gpu 的 11 条指令里，绝大多数（ADD / SUB / MUL / DIV / CMP / CONST / BRnzp / NOP）是 **同步指令**——数据已经躺在寄存器里，ALU 一拍就能算完。只有 LDR / STR 是 **异步访存**——它们要请 LSU 去外部 data 内存取/存数据，而外部内存经由 controller 中继、响应时间不固定（详见 [u3-l2](u3-l2-memory-controller.md)）。

scheduler 的状态机之所以专门设计一个 `WAIT` 阶段，就是为了把「等不等内存」这件事统一抽象出来：是同步指令就 1 拍走过，是异步访存就一直等到所有 LSU 都收到应答为止。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [src/scheduler.sv](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/src/scheduler.sv) | core 的控制流状态机 | **本讲主角**：七阶段定义与每个阶段的转移条件 |
| [src/core.sv](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/src/core.sv) | 计算核心 | scheduler 如何被实例化、`core_state` 如何广播给各子模块 |
| [src/fetcher.sv](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/src/fetcher.sv) | 取指单元 | FETCH 阶段等待的 `fetcher_state == FETCHED` 从何而来 |
| [src/lsu.sv](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/src/lsu.sv) | 访存单元 | WAIT 阶段轮询的 `lsu_state` 四个取值 |
| [src/pc.sv](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/src/pc.sv) | 程序计数器 | UPDATE 阶段读取的 `next_pc` 是如何算出的 |
| [test/helpers/format.py](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/test/helpers/format.py) | 仿真轨迹格式化 | 把 3 位 `core_state` 翻译成可读字符串，供实践时读日志 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 scheduler 的职责与七阶段状态机定义

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

一句话定位：**scheduler 把「执行一条指令」这件事，切成一段固定的流水节拍。**

它只解决一个问题——「现在轮到哪个子模块工作」。它把答案写进一个 3 位输出信号 `core_state`，core 里所有子模块（fetcher / decoder / LSU / ALU / registers / PC）都根据 `core_state` 决定自己这一拍要不要动。这种「单指令流驱动多数据通路」正是 SIMD（单指令多数据）的核心思想——同一个 `core_state` 同时驱动 block 内所有线程的执行单元。

scheduler 处理的粒度是 **一个 block**：dispatcher 给 core 派活后，scheduler 就从这个 block 的第一条指令（PC=0）开始，一条一条地跑，直到遇到 `RET` 指令为止。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

源码顶部的注释把整条指令的生命周期写得很清楚（[src/scheduler.sv:1-15](https://github.com/adam-maj/tiny-gpu/blob/02b6c2ce223f606051a6d3a35ca942fbb1dffde2/src/scheduler.sv#L1-L15)）。一条指令要依次穿过七个阶段，外加首尾两个「空闲/结束」态：

```
        start=1                        fetcher_state==FETCHED
  IDLE ─────────► FETCH ─────────────────────────► DECODE
   ▲                                                    │
   │                                              (1拍) │
   │ reset                                              ▼
  DONE ◄── UPDATE ◄── EXECUTE ◄── WAIT ◄── REQUEST ◄──┘
